about: The differences between the Node server and the Rust server that the specification declares, one entry per request or path, each naming its row of the table in docs/specs/2026-11-27-mcp-server-in-rust.md. A run fails when an entry no longer differs. Unlike the other known-difference lists this one grows with the table; an entry without a row and a reason is refused.

A file whose bytes are not source text (binary data under a source extension) is reported as unresolved with the reason `source-not-parsed` and no imports; the JavaScript server read the bytes as text and reported whatever import-shaped text it found (row 33).

Imports are read from the syntax tree, so a Rust `mod` after an inner attribute, a `use` under `#[cfg]`, a `use` path split over lines and a Java or Kotlin name in any script or inside a string template are found, and a `use` inside a macro body is not; the line scanners lost the first four and read the fifth (row 34, an instance of row 2).

Imports are read from the syntax tree, so a Rust `mod` after an inner attribute, a `use` under `#[cfg]`, a `use` path split over lines and a Java or Kotlin name in any script or inside a string template are found, and a `use` inside a macro body is not; the line scanners lost the first four and read the fifth (row 34, an instance of row 2).

Imports are read from the syntax tree: import-shaped text inside a comment or a string literal is no import, and `import('./x').T` in a type position is `type_only`; the line scanner read both comment and string text as imports and counted the type position as a value (row 34, an instance of row 2).
